root_idea.summary: A root orientation toward settling, remaining still, or resting in place.
root_idea.development: This orientation develops into sleep and the sleeper, while Form V describes rousing oneself from sleep for night prayer. It also appears in the image of a camel settling the front of its neck on the ground.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied Quran occurrence is a Form V verb and has a distinct Quran-attested night-prayer use.

senses.definition: To awaken from sleep for night prayer; to engage in night worship by relinquishing sleep.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ, the Qur'an is understood as the means or occasion of awakening. The use denotes rousing oneself for night prayer, rather than merely remaining awake.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of sleeping at night; one account specifies the latter part of the night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain awake or wakeful at night; to awaken from sleep for a purpose, including prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is recorded as a contrary usage to sleeping. Night prayer and relinquishing sleep are associated with this wakeful branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or cause someone to sleep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive causative use of Form II.
A contrary transitive use of Form II.
Transitive Form IV use; the lexical meaning is not restricted to a particular gender or social class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to lay the front part of its neck on the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific animal posture described with the camel as subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sleeper; one who is sleeping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participle noun associated with the sleeping sense of هَجَدَ.
An active-participle use distinct from the sleeping sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry used to chide a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source records variant vocalizations of the cry.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Wakefulness, awakening, and night-prayer branches, including the Quran-attested construction.

cautions: Classical usage records opposed sleep and wakefulness senses for هَجَدَ and related forms, so derivational form and context are significant.
The Quranic occurrence is an imperative surface form; the public headword is normalized to the Form V perfect citation form.
